title: Debating in the World of AI
author: Stefan Bauschard
summary: Bauschard argues that as AI makes written work unverifiable, schools should lean on things that transcend AI, and classroom debate is the prime example. He says education will not carry on as it is because students can already learn outside the system cheaply. He lists the benefits of debate: performative assessment that a chatbot cannot do for the student, a coaching-team model of human-computer collaboration, practice in relating to smarter machines, and development of courage, patience and kindness. He adds that debate teaches learning to learn, conversation and communication, skills employers say they need. The move is to answer AI disruption by revisiting an old, proven pedagogy rather than overhauling everything.
points: Debate is a performative assessment in which students must answer opponents and synthesize live, which an AI cannot do for them.
The structure of debate teams, with layered coaches and technology, models how humans can work with smarter machines.
Debate builds necessary human attributes such as courage, responsibility, patience and kindness.
Debate teaches learning to learn, a survival skill as industries change quickly.
Employers rank collaboration and communication first, which debate directly develops.
quotes: The reality is that AI is here; it’s not going anywhere. It's getting a lot better. It's going to change the world. It's going to change your classroom. If it doesn't change your classroom, then I don't know what relevance your classroom is going to have to the world.

The idea that education will continue the way it is now in this world and still be relevant is unlikely. OK, I’ll be blunt: it’s not going to carry on the way it is now. If it tries, students will choose learning opportunities outside the current system that are rapidly developing and are very inexpensive. This is already happening.

We don’t know what our students are writing (as compared to machines), but we do know what they are saying in debate tournaments and in-class debates. They can use “ChatGPT” to help write their speeches, but ChatGPT can’t answer questions from opponents in debate, synthesize ideas in debates, or deliver their powerful closing statements.
The best debate teams are structured with a director, a head coach, multiple assistant coaches, layers of debaters (beginners, “JV”, “varsity”), and, nowadays, technology.
I mean attributes such as courage, an ability to collaborate (with humans and machines), responsibility, patience, kindness, resilience, and caring. These are not things we can outsource to machines.

After you debate for a while, you can “crunch” a new topic on your own. Given the rate of change, “adults” will need to be able to do this to thrive. Entire industries will come and go in very short periods of time. If you can’t learn to learn, you are toast.
The premium placed on intelligence will decline in a world of intelligent machines. That is a reality, but the value of these other attributes will increase.
